children: The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 600 crore and an offer for sale OFS worth Rs 400 crore

Hero Motors, an automotive components and advanced mobility manufacturer, has raised nearly Rs 300 crore from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its Rs 1,000 crore initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday.

The company allotted 3.57 crore equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 84 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band. The anchor book saw participation from institutional investors including ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Edelweiss Life Insurance, 3P India Equity Fund, Societe Generale and ASAS Global Fund.
Among mutual fund investors, Hero Motors allocated shares to schemes including ICICI Prudential Smallcap Fund, Kotak MNC Fund and JM Flexi Cap Fund. The IPO will remain open until September 18.

Hero Motors has fixed the price band at Rs 79-84 per share, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 3,815 crore at the upper end. The lot size is 178 shares, translating into a minimum retail investment of Rs 14,952.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 600 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 400 crore. Following the offer, promoter holding is expected to decline to 61.63 per cent from 85.57 per cent.
Of the issue, 35 per cent has been reserved for retail investors and 50 per cent for qualified institutional buyers, with the balance allocated to non-institutional investors.

Hero Motors is commanding a grey market premium of around Rs 19 per share, or roughly 23 per cent over the upper end of the issue price band. However, GMPs are unofficial indicators of activity in the unlisted market and can change sharply. They should not be treated as a reliable indication of the eventual listing price.
Debt Repayment, Capacity Expansion On Agenda

Hero Motors plans to use Rs 190 crore from the fresh issue to repay debt, while another Rs 200 crore will go towards purchasing equipment for capacity expansion at its Gautam Buddha Nagar facility in Uttar Pradesh.
The remaining proceeds will be used for potential acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

The company designs and manufactures powertrain solutions for automotive original equipment manufacturers across the US, Europe, India and the ASEAN region. Its portfolio spans electric and conventional applications across two-wheelers, e-bikes, passenger and commercial vehicles, off-road vehicles and electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft.

Its products include continuously variable transmissions, electric transmissions, electric motors, integrated drive units and gear sets. BMW AG, Ducati Motor Holding, Enviolo International, Formula Motorsport, HUMMINGBIRDEV and HWA AG are among its customers.
Hero Motors reported total income of Rs 1,216.74 crore in FY26, up 9 per cent from Rs 1,111.23 crore in FY25. Profit after tax rose 26 per cent to Rs 41.17 crore from Rs 32.80 crore.
The company is positioning the IPO to support capacity expansion and balance-sheet improvement while also keeping capital available for inorganic growth.
ICICI Securities, DAM Capital Advisors and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.
The IPO is scheduled to close on September 18, with allotment expected on September 21 and the shares proposed to list on the NSE and BSE on September 23.
